measurement: trivial-baseline ceiling, run BEFORE any substrate arm existed
verdict: THE INSTRUMENT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE. A ~20-line scope-filter-plus-interval-containment rule (`scoped_interval`) scores 1.0000 on all 2,115 probes and on all three bands, including the discriminating band where every recency baseline scores 0.0000. Headroom above the trivial baseline is exactly 0.0000, so no substrate arm can win anything here at any n. Do not build the session synthesiser, the probe generator, or the executable harness costed in survey section 4b.7.

probes.cluster_unit: BCD feature (arcs for the same feature across browsers share a cluster)
probes.construction: For each of the 705 strict removed-then-re-added arcs (feature, browser, live_from L, removed_at R, readded_at A): B1 asks at L <= V < R (gold supported), B2 at R <= V < A (gold NOT supported), B3 at V >= A (gold supported). B2 is the discriminating band: the newest assertion about the feature is the wrong answer there.
probes.gold_provenance: BCD's own version intervals, verbatim. No gold authored here.

robustness_interior_query_versions_only.why: the query version is never a declared version, so no rule can win by exact match

the_good_half_of_the_result: BCD does what the survey promised on the recency axis: constant, mode, latest-declared and max-version ALL score exactly 0.0000 on the discriminating band. That is a strictly stronger property than MemoryCode, whose gold is recency-identified by construction. It is simply not sufficient, which is precisely S6's lesson repeated on a second corpus.
why_this_is_structural_not_an_authoring_: BCD's gold IS interval containment on a totally ordered (browser, version) key, and the probe is indexed by that same key. Any probe whose gold derives from BCD's intervals is by construction answerable by evaluating them. A substrate could only beat the 20-line rule if our authored episode wording obscured scope or version enough to make extraction hard -- at which point the difficulty is authored by us (the self-mined class this program discounts) and the thing measured is extraction, not memory semantics. On this corpus, 'discriminating' and 'inherited gold' are mutually exclusive.
decisional_false_reason: n_d = 0 against the saturating baseline, which is below the n_d >= 6 floor, so this artifact may not carry a promotion decision and is not claiming one. It is an EXHAUSTIVE CEILING CENSUS over the full arc set, not a sampled paired test: the kill follows from a deterministic score of 1.0000 on every probe, not from a failed significance test. Recording it as decisional=true would weaken the very guard that exists to stop nulls being read as results.

evidence_contract.claim: On 2,115 probes mined from the 705 strict removed-then-re-added arcs in MDN browser-compat-data v8.0.8, a ~20-line scope-filtered interval-containment rule that touches no substrate scores 1.0000 overall and 1.0000 on the discriminating band, leaving exactly zero headroom for any memory arm.

evidence_contract.mechanism_evidence: No MemPhant mechanism was enabled and none was intended: no server, no scratch database, no embedding model, no recall path. This artifact measures only substrate-free read rules, which is the point -- it is the gate that decides whether running a mechanism here is worth anything, and it says no.

harness.scorer: exact match against BCD's own interval containment; deterministic, no judge, no model call

instrument_verification.false_positive_gate: Survey section 4b.4 requires reproducing the ~75%-false-positive naive arc query. Reproduced: the naive removed-then-added query returns 1,553 features / 5,079 pairs; the strict filter (no flags / prefix / alternative_name / partial_implementation, strict version gap) returns 326 / 705, a 79.0% false-positive rate. Yield stated as 326 features / 705 browser-pairs against the survey's 325 / 704 -- one more feature and one more pair, in nodejs, disclosed and not reconciled by tuning a threshold.
